chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hamdan ibn Suleyman, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani, from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus ibn Abi Wahb al-Qasri, who said:

I entered Medina, so I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I came to you and I have not performed the Ziyarah of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Bad is what you have done. Had you not been from our Shiah, I would not have looked at you. Do you not visit the one whom Allah visits along with the Angels, and the Prophets visit him, and the believers visit him?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I had no knowledge of that.' He said: 'Know that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) is superior in the Presence of Allah than all the Imams, and for him is the reward of their deeds, and they are distinguished according to the measure of their deeds.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of visiting Imam Ali (AS) according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the narrator’s assumption that visiting the Prophet suffices, elevating the Ziyarah of Imam Ali (AS) as a prerequisite for true Shia identity. The text establishes a unique theological hierarchy where Imam Ali (AS) is superior to all other Imams, possessing the cumulative reward of their collective deeds, a concept central to Shia understanding of the Imamate's spiritual authority. This underscores the practical implication that honoring the Commander of the Faithful is essential for accessing the merits of the entire Ahl al-Bayt.
